decision: NX-030 D3 (owner 2026-10-10, all as recommended): default thresholds of design §2. Evaluated once a minute on the SQL snapshot, world 'real' only (D6); one alert per rule and selector, resolved when the condition clears; shown to the owner in the workbench (D2). metric is a dotted path into runtime.nexloop_metrics_snapshot; one '*' segment iterates its children (the child key becomes the selector); selector picks one key of a map. A new version is a new file. v2 (relay multi-consumer, 0160): relay_unenrolled_pending — inbound messages of a consumer that no relay is enrolled to serve would never get a message Run (critical after 5 minutes, so an enrollment in progress does not fire); relay_backlog_age — the oldest inbound message still waiting for a relay (warning, same 10 minutes as the queue backlog). v3 (NX-035 local part, 0146): the M12 backup block is wired to the backup manifest — backup_age reads backup.age_seconds (the latest verified PG backup, unchanged rule); new: wal_archive_lag and wal_archive_failing (RPO ≤ 5 minutes, D2), offsite_backup_age (repo2, once enabled, D3), file_backup_age (D2 file RPO 15 minutes, alert at 1 hour), restore_journal_lag (§6.2), restore_drill_overdue (35 days, D6; counted from the first verified backup while no drill has passed) and backup_verify_failed (§3.2). A metric without an observation is absent, never zero. v4 (NX-037 provider routing): effect_route_unconfigured, a warning when an effect intent of an Action without a provider route was refused (NXE01). v5 (dispatcher 2026-10-18, claim-matcher idle): candidates_without_merge_configuration, a warning when staged candidate definitions wait for 10 minutes while the tenant has no active merge configuration (0216 candidates block; apply deploy/ontology/merge-config.v1.json through nexloop_eios.merge_configuration --apply). v6 (data health, D-G5): thresholds on the snapshot block data_health (NexLoop's own data flows: extraction, recall index, review reflow, ingestion, Artifacts, erasure propagation); counts and ages only. v7 (NX-039 V5, owner D39-10 2026-10-20): evolution_release_regressing, a warning when a semantic release in its 7-day watch window shows a miss rate or an ambiguity rate more than 2 points above the week before publication (at least 20 accesses on each side; evolution.release_watch in the snapshot). It suggests a rollback in the workbench; nothing rolls back automatically. v8 (outreach slice 8): thresholds on the snapshot block outreach (proactive outreach metrics; counts and ratios only). v9 (NX-040 F4, owner D27 2026-10-20): schema_release_regressing, a warning when a Schema publication in its 7-day watch shows a claim-extraction failure rate more than 2 points above the week before (at least 20 tasks a side) or a Context volume above 105% (at least 20 packs a side) (evolution.schema_watch). It suggests the next, hidden version; nothing rolls back automatically. v10 (L6, stage clock skew 2026-10-20): clock_skew - the APP_HOST clock against the database clock, measured by the alert evaluator before each evaluation; above 2 s (signed commands tolerate 5 s) the hosts must be brought back in sync. v11 (NX-043 X5, dispatcher 2026-10-21): v10 plus experiment_auto_stopped - a guardrail stopped an experiment in the last 24 hours (warning); the owner reads the stop reason in the experiment record. v13 (NX-061 B9, aligned with the host health scheduled-run caliber of v12): timer_stale_file_backup - no scheduled successful run of the APP_HOST file backup (every 15 minutes) for 45 minutes; a manual nexloop-file-backup run refreshes backup.file_backup_age_seconds but not this, so a failing scheduled round stays visible. It needs the timer in APP_HOST's host-health configuration (name file-backup); without that key it never fires. v14 (NX-056 A3/A7): v13 plus the unified approval rules - approval_waiting, approval_unconsumed, approval_sweep_stale and the single-person mode's approval_solo_mode, approval_solo_self_approved, approval_solo_eligibility_reduced (metrics block 'approvals'). v15 (NX-057 R1/R2, remediation intents; v14 is NX-056's): v14 plus remediation_waiting - a remediation proposed, or escalated to the owner, more than 24 hours ago still waits for the owner (warning); remediation_rate_capped - the tenant reached its hourly remediation limit and the excess was aggregated into one escalation (warning); remediation_paused - the owner paused remediation for the tenant (warning: the design's info severity is not supported by the alert path); remediation_rule_held - the breaker held a rule (critical). remediation_failed comes with R3 (governed_action). v16 (NX-056 B1, ADR-039 §6.6; batch 27): v15 plus approval_first_time_approver (a member's first approve vote in the tenant, last 24 hours) and approval_same_person_flag (NX-058 slice D's same-person flag on an owner invitation; 0 before it). L3 drafted these as v15 alongside NX-057's v15; the batch publishes them as v16. v17 (feed backlog review, L6 2026-10-26; migration feed_backlog_due): v16 plus feed_attempts_over_ceiling - a pending work feed item above 20 attempts. A retry dead-letters an item at attempts >= its ceiling and SQL bounds every ceiling at 20 (0093), so above 20 the item was claimed without an outcome at least once: its worker died after claiming it and it is claimed again at each lease expiry, never dead-lettered (critical, like feed_dead_letter). One threshold for every feed: the ceilings are per worker and per refusal code (1 to 20: reply-due min(20, fallback + 5), plan-reevaluate 20 when throttled, takeover-expiry 20), not in the database, and a feed name cannot be written in a metric path (hyphens); below 20 a feed's own ceiling cannot be told from a legitimate retry. v18 (extraction dead letters; v17 is L7's feed attempts rule, merged at batch time; docs/release/run-extraction-dead-letters-diagnosis.md): v17 with data_health_extraction_dead_letters moved to data_health.extraction.unresolved_dead_letters - dead letters with no owner decision (claim_extraction.dead_letter_resolve: requeue or dismiss) and not fully covered by a later succeeded extraction of the same conversation; dead_lettered_total keeps every dead letter for reference. No other rule changes from v17. v19 (NX-054 P4a, dispatcher 2026-10-26): timer_stale_relation_read_gaps - the daily relation read gap check on DATA_HOST (nexloop-relation-read-gaps.timer, 03:40) has its scheduled-run freshness rule like the other timers (26 h: a day plus margin); its failures (gaps > 0, unwritten evidence) are timer_scheduled_failure. A P5 precondition (docs/design/relation-read-p4.md §2.5). Also in v19 (NX-061 E4, owner decision relayed by the dispatcher 2026-10-26): api_read_p95_high - the API's read class p95 (api.classes.read.p95_ms, the 5-minute merged histogram of every API process, 0323) above 500 ms, the PRD 8 read target, for 10 minutes. v20 (NX-035 D6, owner 2026-10-26; migration file_backup_unprotected): v19 plus file_backup_unprotected - for the tenant, an object the file backup inventory lists (an available Artifact inside its retention, a finished Run not queued for a purge, world real) became backupable more than an hour ago and no verified file snapshot of its kind started after that: none was ever taken, or the backup stopped while new data arrived (backup.file_backup_unprotected_seconds; absent while everything is covered). file_backup_age never fires before a first verified file snapshot; this one does. No other rule changes from v19. v21 (NX-035 repo2 maintenance, dispatcher 2026-10-26 option 甲): v20 plus timer_stale_file_backup_maint - no scheduled successful run of nexloop-file-backup-maint.timer on APP_HOST (repo2 of the file backup: forget per tag with --prune, check; daily 04:07) for 26 hours (a day plus margin, like restic-maint); its failures are timer_scheduled_failure. Without it repo2's file snapshots would grow without bound unnoticed. It needs file-backup-maint in APP_HOST's host-health configuration (file_backup_install.sh step 6). No other rule changes from v20. v22 (world-model glossary, owner 2026-10-29): v21 plus timer_stale_world_glossary - no scheduled successful run of nexloop-world-glossary.timer on APP_HOST (the translator's --once run every 10 minutes) for 30 minutes; fail closed when none was ever seen (host-health); its failures are timer_scheduled_failure. It needs world-glossary in APP_HOST's host-health configuration. Also (I7, so a timer that keeps succeeding cannot hide failing translations): world_glossary_failed - a translation job reached failed (three attempts) in the last 24 hours; world_glossary_no_success - jobs wait while the last 24 hours had at least three model calls and not one wrote a gloss (metrics block world_glossary, migration 0374). Both warnings. No other rule changes from v21. v23 (L6 S43/S45, dispatcher 2026-10-30; after the stage relay assembly expired unnoticed on 10-22): five rules on the relay_readiness block (migration relay_dependency_expiry): relay_dependency_expiring - a dependency of an active relay enrollment (EffectControl and its ledger row, offering, binding, enterprise slot, role definition/link/step, the step's Goal, the role's ceiling and the link's scope) has valid_until within 7 days, warning; relay_dependency_expired - one has passed or is missing, critical; relay_unserviceable_enrollment - an active enrollment's relay profile is null (claim_next skips it), critical after 60 s; relay_no_active_enrollment - the tenant has no active enrollment at all (nothing for the relay to serve is shown, never a silent zero), warning after 10 minutes; relay_stalled_consumers - an enrolled consumer's oldest pending message waited more than 5 minutes with no relay lease (the relay ticks idle past it), warning after 5 minutes. No other rule changes from v22. v24 (I29 / L6 S60, 2026-10-31): semantic_read_no_readable_types - a semantic access in the last hour whose caller could read no definition type at all (miss_reason no_readable_types; metrics block semantic_reads from migration semantic_read_health), warning at once: the R60 relay read every statement against an empty definition scope and nothing said so. No other rule changes from v23. v25 (I31, dispatcher 2026-10-31; after three stage service credentials were found to expire on 2026-11-04 with no alert): two rules on the service_credentials block (migration service_credential_rotation): service_credential_expiring - an active service token of the world expires within 7 days, warning (renew it with stage_secrets.py rotate-credential; a rotation's previous token keeps this until revoke-credential --previous); service_credential_expired - an active service token has passed its expiry (its service is refused at authentication), critical. No other rule changes from v24. v26 (stale action claims, dispatcher 2026-10-31; batch 71: on v25, L4 I31's service credential rules): action_claim_stale - an action claim stayed active more than an hour past its lease (action_claims.stale_active_oldest_age_seconds; metrics block action_claims from migration action_claim_settle), warning: fifteen were found by hand on stage 10-31; a postgres claim is settled with nexloop.action_claim.settle (uncommitted), an effect claim is reconciled first. action_claim_stale_effect - an effect Action's claim (target system not postgres) stale for 15 minutes, critical: its external result may be unknown and needs a query, never a resend. No other rule changes from v25. v27 (I35-g / I36-e, dispatcher 2026-10-31; L6's findings, batch 73): two warnings on v26. workbench_read_types_missing - the tenant has a workbench configuration and its current roles version has no read lists (workbench_read_types.missing, a number: the evaluator compares numbers only, so the block's boolean present would never fire; migration workbench_read_types): the owner is back at the 0123/0224 reads without a sign; rerun workbench_roles --apply. A tenant without a workbench configuration reports {configured: false, missing: 0}, a visible zero, and does not fire. commitment_orphan_seen - the commitment keeper met a commitment with no registry row in the last 24 hours (commitment_orphans.seen_last_24h; migration erasure_cancels_undated_commitments counts every orphan it records, 0 when there is none): a tenant-context or RLS fault hiding registry rows shows here instead of passing silently. No other rule changes from v26. v28 (S86 step 1, owner 2026-11-01; after the D1 calibration: the pack estimate counts about half of the provider input): two rules on the context_input_ratio block (migration context_input_ratio): for each model and Run kind over the last 24 hours, the provider input of a model request (usage input + cache_read + cache_write) against the strategy's input_token_budget. context_input_ratio_p95 - p95 at or above 0.9, warning: the Contexts of that kind are near the budget the strategy set; context_input_ratio_max - one request at or above 1.0, critical: a request was sent above its input budget. Without a measured request the block says present: false and has no ratio (the rules see nothing, the snapshot says why); configured says whether the tenant has a published Context strategy. context_input_usage_missing - a succeeded model request of the last 24 hours has no numeric provider usage (requests_without_usage_24h, always a number), warning: the ratio cannot be measured for it, so requests without usage never look like no requests (L6 M1). No other rule changes from v27. v29 (NX-064, design v2 and ADR-029c, L6 C2/C3): the effect_requests block (migration effect_request_metrics) over 24 hours, from process samples only (never a log). Three items judged apart, each no data on its own: effect_submit_no_data, effect_find_no_data (no guard_op sample of that operation) and host_effect_no_data (no 'host' sample carrying the Host's effect counters: a Host before NX-064 or a stopped sampler), warnings - no data is never a pass. effect_submit_over_2s and effect_find_over_2s: more than 1% of the calls reached the guard's 2 s deadline, warning. host_effect_unavailable: an effect request of the Host ended unavailable, warning. enterprise_deliver_unavailable: a Run's nexloop.enterprise.deliver ended runtime_effect_unavailable, critical, on its own for the owner with the run ids (effect_requests.enterprise_unavailable.run_ids): either (a) the order was placed but the customer was not told (the guard committed the intent after the Host gave up; the Run failed before the model saw the result) or (b) there is no order; the owner checks the intent list by run id. Notice only: nothing re-orders automatically. No other rule changes from v28. v30 (L6 follow-up to S-DUP, dispatcher 2026-11-03; migration extraction_failed_codes): a claim-extraction job that ends failed is never retried and raised no alert; the data_health extraction block now counts failed jobs of 24 hours by code (failed_24h). extraction_context_cited - the recorder refused a Claim citing a context Message (context_cited_24h > 0), warning: the client filter that drops such Claims failed and that window's Claims were lost. extraction_no_data - new input waited for extraction in the last 24 hours (feed rows or pending jobs) but no claim-extraction job ended (no_data), warning: the failure counts measured nothing, which is not a pass. With no input at all the block says idle: 1 and no_data: 0 (no alert on a quiet tenant); a stopped worker with pending jobs is also queue_backlog_age. No other rule changes from v29. v31 (NX-061 B5 threshold, owner 2026-11-07 as recommended, relayed by the dispatcher; migration outcome_failure_rate_gate): outcomes_failure_rate_high - in the last hour at least 10 outcomes were decided and the failure rate (transient, authorization, defect and unresolved over decided; refusals by rule are not failures, 0324) is above 0.2, warning. The evaluator compares one number, so the snapshot carries outcomes.failure_rate_gated: the rate when decided >= 10, null otherwise. Fewer than 10 decided is insufficient data (outcomes.gate insufficient_data, outcomes.insufficient_data 1): not judged and not a pass, shown in the snapshot and raising no alert, as the owner chose; no snapshot or no outcomes block is no data, likewise never a pass. The thresholds are revisited on real data after go-live. No other rule changes from v30. v32 (budget health, dispatcher 2026-11-07; after the stage model budget's period ended 11-05 16:00Z with no alert for two days; migration budget_health): four rules on the snapshot block budget_health; its required kinds are model always and evolution once the tenant takes part in evolution (a principal in authz.nexloop_evo_principals or an evolution budget row; budget_health.required lists them). budget_expiring - a configured budget's period ends within 7 days (budget_health.expiring_7d), warning: renew it before it ends. budget_expired - a configured budget is outside its period (budget_health.expired; ended, or not yet started), critical: every reservation of that kind is refused (NXB01 budget period closed), customer conversations end with the fallback reply. budget_unconfigured - a required kind has no budget row (budget_health.unconfigured), critical: an absent budget is never a silent pass. budget_exhausted_recent - an NXB01 budget refusal in the last hour (budget_health.exhausted_refusals_1h), critical: the 5-minute refusal_budget_exhausted window opens and closes with sparse traffic. No other rule changes from v31. v33 (NX-055 E3 on stage 2026-11-08: two watched timers were never installed, so their keys were absent and timer_stale_* never fired; migration timers_not_reported): timer_not_reported - a timer a timer_stale_ rule of the tenant's applied rules watches has no value in host_health.timer_success_age_seconds (host_health.timers_not_reported, the names in timers_not_reported_names), warning: the timer is not installed or not in its host's probe configuration. Install it and list it in the host-health configuration, or drop its timer_stale_ rule in a new rules version. No other rule changes from v32. v34 (owner 2026-11-08, docs/implementation/alert-notifier-design.md): timer_stale_alert_notify - the out-of-workbench alert notifier's own scheduled run (every 15 minutes) is watched like every other timer; nothing else changes. v35 (NX-062 M3, L6 C4 and ADR-041 §2.2 T-1): machine_rate_policy_missing - no machine rate policy is in force, so every machine request is refused and counted (critical: the machine channel is closed, never unlimited); machine_key_denials - more than 50 machine requests in 24 hours whose key did not authenticate (warning: a leaked, revoked or guessed key; the owner can revoke at once). The thresholds live here, never in code. No other rule changes from v34. v36 (D23 option B, L6 J1 on 944be8b5): action_input_shadow_failures - an input-schema shadow validation that could not run (authz.nexloop_action_input_shadow_failure, migration action_input_tenant_narrow) leaves dispatch untouched and counts nothing, so its counts may be missing; warning on any such failure within 24 hours.

rules.purpose: M01: model or incentive budget exhausted; new work is being refused.
M01: many dispatches refused for a stale control revision; reevaluation is not keeping up.
M01: many dispatches refused for a superseded goal version.
M02: an external result has been unknown for more than 15 minutes; query, never resend.
M02: an external result has been unknown for more than 2 hours.
M03: reconciliation left an effect unknown for more than 24 hours.
M04: a fallback reply failed or did not start (ADR-023: every inbound message gets a reply).
M05: a commitment passed its due date unfulfilled.
M05: a commitment was made to a contact-restricted customer.
M06: a queued task was dead-lettered.
M06: the oldest due task has waited more than 10 minutes.
M06: a work feed item was dead-lettered.
M06/M07: a work feed has waited more than 10 minutes.
M07: an accepted message has waited more than 30 minutes for extraction.
M08: more than 1% of guard calls hit the 2 s deadline in the last 5 minutes.
M08: guard p95 above 1500 ms, close to the 2 s deadline.
M09: a Run waited past the Agent Host admission window (runtime_capacity_exhausted).
M10: connection pool requests have been waiting for 5 minutes.
M10: more than 50 database connections (deployment limit 60).
M11: more than 80% of a budget used (the limit itself is enforced by NX-022).
M12: last backup older than 26 hours (wired when NX-035 provides the backup manifest; unavailable until then).
Relay multi-consumer: pending inbound messages of consumers without an active relay enrollment; no relay will serve them.
Relay multi-consumer: the oldest inbound message still waiting for a relay.
M12: no WAL segment archived for more than 5 minutes; the database RPO of 5 minutes (D2) is at risk.
M12: the latest WAL archive attempt failed after the latest success.
M12: the latest verified backup in the offsite repository (repo2) is older than 26 hours (D3; evaluated once repo2 holds a backup).
M12: the latest verified file snapshot (Artifacts, finished Runs) is older than 1 hour (file RPO 15 minutes, D2).
M12: a restore-journal entry (deletion, contact restriction, revocation) has waited more than 5 minutes for export; a restore could lose it (design §6.2).
M12: no passed restore drill for more than 35 days (D6).
M12: the latest PG backup failed its verification.
NX-037: an effect intent's Action has no provider route in the effect worker; it is not dispatched until the route is configured.
NX-045: staged candidate definitions cannot be glued because the tenant has no active merge configuration; the claim-matcher stays idle (merge_configuration_missing).

D-G5: claim-extraction jobs ended in the dead letter state that no later extraction of the conversation fully covered and the owner has not resolved; their messages may have no Claims until the owner requeues or dismisses them (workbench data health).
D-G5: an inbound message has waited more than an hour for claim extraction (feed not enqueued).
D-G5: recall entries without an embedding under the active profile for an hour; recall misses them until a backfill runs.
D-G5: vectors under a profile other than the active one remain for a day (profile change not yet backfilled or cleaned).
D-G5: a review decision has waited more than an hour for its Claims to reflow.
D-G5: signed commercial events rejected for their signature in the last 24 hours (key rotation or a forged sender).
D-G5: available Artifacts older than a day that no Context binding, Role Context or erasure record references.
D-G5: Artifacts in the deleting state for more than an hour.
D-G5: a Consumer erasure has not finished within a day.
D-G5: Run purge items of an erasure or retention expiry retried three times or more.
D39-10: a semantic release in its 7-day watch is worse than the week before (miss or ambiguity rate up more than 2 points); consider a rollback - never automatic.
Outreach slice 8: more than 5% of marketing sends of the last 7 days were followed by an unsubscribe (reported only from 20 marketing sends on); review the marketing purposes, wording and allowance.
Outreach slice 6/8: proactive sends have waited for approval for 12 hours; approve or reject them before their window closes.
D27: a Schema publication in its 7-day watch is worse (extraction failures up more than 2 points, or Context volume above 105%); consider publishing the hidden version - never automatic.
APP_HOST and the database clocks differ by more than 2 s (midpoint of a round trip); signed commands are refused beyond 5 s. Align the NTP sources of the hosts.

NX-043 X5: a guardrail (refusal rate, reconciliation anomaly, budget, withdrawn twin, reclassified purpose, end time) stopped an experiment; every participant is back on the control strategy. Read the reason and the metrics in the experiment record before registering a new experiment.
E2: a container or service restarted 3 or more times in the last hour (restart count deltas from the host probe, not from the service); 'running' alone hides a crash loop.
E2/E3: the host probe has not recorded for 5 minutes; crash-loop and timer freshness rules see nothing (not seeing is not healthy).
E2: the last probe tick saw none (or under half) of the units it expects: docker or systemd unreadable; zero restarts would not mean healthy.
E2 (L6 review I2): a configured container or service was not seen by the host probe's last tick (removed, renamed or unreadable); its restarts would otherwise silently disappear.
E3: a scheduled timer run failed in the last 24 hours (a manual rerun does not clear it).

E3: no scheduled successful run of the differential PG backup (Mon-Sat 02:00; Saturday to Monday is 48 hours) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
E3: no scheduled successful run of the weekly full PG backup (Sunday 02:00) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
E3: no scheduled successful run of the restore journal export (every minute) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
E3: no scheduled successful run of the restore journal to restic repo1 (every 5 minutes) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
E3: no scheduled successful run of the restore journal to restic repo2 (every 15 minutes) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
E3: no scheduled successful run of the restic forget/prune/check (daily 03:30) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
E3: no scheduled successful run of the provider drift check (hourly) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
World-model glossary: no scheduled successful run of the translator timer (every 10 minutes) for three periods; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
World-model glossary: a translation job failed three times in the last 24 hours (the identifier shows English only); check the model key and provider, the owner may also set the gloss by hand.

World-model glossary: identifiers wait while the last 24 hours had at least three model calls and none wrote a gloss (a revoked key or a provider that always refuses); the timer still succeeds, so this is the signal.
B9: no scheduled successful run of the file backup (every 15 minutes) for three periods; a manual rerun does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
NX-056 A3: an approval has waited for a decision for more than an hour (it expires at its due_by, 24 hours by default); the eligible approvers see it under the workbench approvals view.
NX-056 A3: an approved request has not been executed by its requester for an hour; it expires unexecuted at its due_by.
NX-056 A3 (L6 review): a request past its due_by is still waiting or approved and unconsumed for 15 minutes; the expiry sweep in the retention keeper is not running.
NX-056 A7 (design §15): the single-person mode is on - the one eligible approver may approve their own requests; check it was meant (a stolen owner session could turn it on).
NX-056 A7: a request was approved by its own requester in the single-person mode within the last 24 hours (audit approval.decided with self_approved).
NX-056 A7: the number of eligible approvers of a policy went down within the last 24 hours (an approver role removed or a member disabled) - the first step of turning two-person control into one.
NX-057: a remediation intent proposed more than 24 hours ago still waits for the owner (mark it handled or cancel it on the Actions page).
NX-057: the tenant reached its hourly remediation limit; the excess failures were aggregated into one escalation instead of one remediation each.
NX-057: remediation is paused for the tenant; final failures of this time get no remediation, now or later.
NX-057: the remediation breaker held a rule (remediation-origin failures or capped escalations past the daily limit); it generates nothing until the owner releases it.
NX-056 B1 (ADR-039 §6.6): someone cast their first approve vote in this tenant within the last 24 hours - check it is a person you expect (an owner-made second identity would show here first).
NX-056 B1 / NX-058 slice D (ADR-039 §6.6): an owner invitation was accepted by the same person who issued it within the last 24 hours.

M06: a pending work feed item has been claimed more than 20 times - more than any retry ceiling allows; its worker claims it and stops without completing or retrying (crash loop), so it never reaches the dead letter.

NX-054 P4a: no scheduled successful run of the daily relation read gap check (03:40) for longer than its period plus margin; a manual run does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen. Its failed runs (gaps, unwritten evidence) are timer_scheduled_failure.

NX-061 E4 (owner decision): the read requests' p95 over the last 5 minutes, merged from every API process's histogram (0323), above the PRD 8 read target of 500 ms for 10 minutes. No value while the API recorded no read sample in the window (api.status not ok) - the probe staleness rules cover a silent API.
D6: an Artifact or finished Run has been backupable for more than 1 hour with no verified file snapshot of its kind after it (never enabled, or stopped); file RPO 15 minutes, D2.
No scheduled successful run of the file backup repo2 maintenance (daily) for a day plus margin; a manual run does not count; fail closed when none was ever seen.
Relay readiness (v23): a dependency of an active relay enrollment expires within 7 days; renew it (re-assemble) before the relay stops serving.
Relay readiness (v23): a dependency of an active relay enrollment has expired or is missing; the relay no longer serves that consumer.
Relay readiness (v23): an active enrollment has no relay profile now (control, ledger, offering or binding invalid); claim_next skips its consumer.
Relay readiness (v23): the tenant has no active relay enrollment; inbound messages have no relay to serve them.
Relay readiness (v23): an enrolled consumer has waited more than 5 minutes with no relay lease: the relay idles past it.
Semantic reads (v24): a semantic access in the last hour could read no definition type (miss_reason no_readable_types): the caller lacks definition READ and every read comes back empty.
Service credentials (v25): an active service token expires within 7 days; renew it (stage_secrets.py rotate-credential) and revoke the previous token.
Service credentials (v25): an active service token has passed its expiry; its service is refused at authentication until a new token is in place.

Stale action claims (2026-10-31): an action claim stayed active more than an hour past its lease; nothing reserves it again. Read the diagnosis, then settle a postgres claim (uncommitted) or reconcile an effect claim first.
